rationale: Colours 1–4 cast up and down in their own colours; overlapping columns become 6. In demonstration 2, the shared column of 4 and 2 becomes 6 while their source cells remain unchanged; 8 casts no rays.

Vertical rays retain source colours and overlapping rays paint 2. Demonstration 1 preserves the 8 between rays from 3 and 4, and demonstration 3 makes every background cell in the column containing two 4s colour 2.

Sources cast along all four diagonals in their own colours, with overlaps coloured 2. Demonstration 2 shows overlapping diagonals from the two 3s becoming 2; demonstration 3 overwrites the non-source 8 with a diagonal ray.

Colours 1–4 extend across their rows and columns, and overlaps become 6. Demonstration 1 overwrites the 8 in column 0 with 1; demonstration 3 preserves the off-ray 8 and makes the shared source row's background cells 6.

All four orthogonal rays use source colours and mark overlaps with 2. Demonstration 1 preserves the 8 on the bottom row while painting beyond it; demonstration 2 turns the shared row of 3 and 1 into 2 except at source cells.

Colours 1–4 cast four diagonal rays, preserving occupied cells and colouring overlaps 6. Demonstration 3 has a 6 at the intersection of diagonals from 2 and 4; demonstration 2 preserves the 3 source along the shared diagonal.

Sources extend left and right in their own colours; multiple rays make 6. Demonstration 1 overwrites the 8 between 4 and 1 with 6, and demonstration 2 makes all non-source cells in the row of two 2s colour 6.

Horizontal rays retain source colours and overlapping rays become 2, skipping occupied cells. Demonstration 1 fills the lone 1's row with 1 and the shared 1-and-4 row with 2 while preserving both sources; 8 casts no rays.

Sources cast right and down, with overlaps becoming 2. Demonstration 2 preserves the 8 immediately right of 4 and continues painting beyond it; the downward ray from 4 also continues through the 3 source to create a 2 below it.

Colours 1–4 cast right and down in their own colours, protecting source cells and marking overlaps 2. Demonstration 1 makes the cells right of the adjacent 3 and 4 become 2; demonstration 3 makes the shared downward column below the two 1s become 2.
